page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.4-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on the x86_64 architecture. The server allocates 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7J13 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.55 GHz, with 2 threads per core under dedicated CPU allocation. It is paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

This instance profile features no bundled local NVMe storage and no discrete hardware accelerators, requiring network-attached block volumes for operating systems and persistent data. The allocation of dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources provides balanced CPU and memory densities without shared-resource contention. This configuration provides predictable baseline computing efficiency across steady-state workloads.

VM.Standard.E4.Flex.4-32 is appropriate for balanced enterprise applications that do not require local solid-state drives or GPU hardware. Typical workload deployments include medium-scale web application serving, backend microservices, enterprise application middleware, development environments, and standard relational database instances backed by remote block storage.
